sections.heading: Who is Raffaele Longo Elia?
paragraphs: I am a Senior Software Engineer based in the Milan area, Italy. I have been working as a software engineer since 2010, building web applications mostly in PHP, and for the last seven years I have focused on Laravel, Vue and system architecture. I own features end to end: analysis, data model, API, front end, automated tests and deployment.

sections.heading: What am I working on right now?
paragraphs: Since September 2024 I have been a Software Engineer at Bene Assicurazioni in Seregno. In a team of four we built a direct-to-consumer car insurance website from scratch, with me as the backend-focused engineer. The platform now processes over €30M in annual premiums and is still growing. I am the lead contributor to its architecture: codebase conventions, REST API design and microservice boundaries, on Laravel 12, MySQL 8, Vue 3, Redis and AWS.

sections.heading: What did I do before that?
paragraphs: From 2017 to 2024 I worked as a consultant for Si2001 SpA, spending seven years on an enterprise engagement in the Customer Operations – Provisioning department of Vodafone Italia. In a team of three we designed and built the department's tooling, which serves thousands of customers per day: reporting dashboards, back-office applications and scheduled processes that notify field technicians across Italy.

My career started in Messina as a full stack developer. At Provy, from 2008, I built Callstation, a contact-centre management system integrated with Asterisk PBX, and moved the PBX to the cloud in 2010. At Artebianca I digitised warehouse operations with a custom management system. After a career break in Australia to reach professional English fluency, I joined Interteck, where I worked on the software behind the Case dell'Acqua water-dispensing kiosks.

sections.heading: How do I like to work?
paragraphs: I like owning a feature from start to finish: understanding the business problem, modelling the data, designing the API, building the Vue front end, covering it with PHPUnit or Pest tests and shipping it through CI/CD. On my current team I am the de facto technical reference, so a good part of my work is defining conventions that keep the codebase consistent as it grows.

sections.heading: Where did I study?
paragraphs: I studied Computer Science at the University of Messina, specialising in computer networks and distributed systems. Those years overlapped with my first job at Provy, and the networking background has stayed useful: in several roles I also looked after company networks alongside the software.

sections.heading: What do I do outside of work?
paragraphs: Outside of work I am into rock music and science, and I keep experimenting with code. My side projects, such as a daily logic puzzle website, Laravel tooling packages and a RAG app builder, are all on GitHub and featured in the projects section of the home page.

sections.heading: Am I open to new roles?
paragraphs: Yes. I live in the Milan area and I am open to full-remote roles across the EU. I speak Italian as my native language and English at C1 level. The quickest way to reach me is LinkedIn, and my open-source work is on GitHub; both are linked at the bottom of every page.

privacyPage.seoDescription: How raffaelelongoelia.dev handles your data: no tracking, one language cookie, GitHub API requests for the projects list and standard hosting logs.
privacyPage.title: Privacy policy

sections.heading: Who runs this site?
paragraphs: This site is the personal portfolio of Raffaele Longo Elia, who is responsible for it. It has no user accounts, no contact forms and no newsletter, so it never asks you to enter personal data.

sections.heading: Does this site track me?
paragraphs: No. There is no analytics, no advertising and no third-party tracking script. Fonts and all other assets are served from this site itself rather than from external services.

sections.heading: Which cookies and local storage are used?
paragraphs: One cookie, i18n_redirected, remembers the language you chose so that you are never redirected against your choice. Your browser may also keep a display preference (colour mode) in local storage. Both are strictly functional, stay on your device and are not used to identify you.

sections.heading: Which third parties receive data?
paragraphs: The terminal's projects command loads the list of public repositories directly from the GitHub API (api.github.com). Your browser connects to GitHub to do this, so GitHub receives your IP address and browser details under its own privacy policy. Links to GitHub and LinkedIn open those sites, which apply their own policies.

sections.heading: What does the hosting provider record?
paragraphs: The site is hosted by OVH. Like any web server, it may keep standard technical logs, such as IP address, date, requested page and browser, for security and operation. These logs are not used for profiling or marketing.

sections.heading: What are my rights?
paragraphs: Under the GDPR you can ask for access to, correction or deletion of personal data concerning you. Since this site does not collect personal data directly, requests about data held by GitHub, LinkedIn or OVH should go to those providers; for anything else, you can contact me on LinkedIn.
